label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores, PHQ-9 depression scores, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below typical thresholds, these individuals demonstrate strong psychological well-being despite moderate daily screen or internet use of 1 to 3 hours.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily internet/screen use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness levels (UCLA-8 mean: 0.79, indicating minimal social isolation)
Minimal depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean: 0.28, far below clinical concern)
Near-absent anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean: 0.04, essentially negligible)
Moderate and controlled internet/screen usage (1–3 hours daily)
Higher educational attainment suggesting structured daily routines and social engagement
tone: Stable, emotionally grounded, and psychologically resilient

label: Digitally Over-Connected & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Despite heavy digital engagement, they experience pronounced emotional distress across all three measured dimensions, with anxiety being the most prominent (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.10), followed by depression (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 1.65) and loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.66). The combination of extensive screen time and graduate-level education suggests individuals who may be immersed in demanding academic or professional digital environments, yet feel socially isolated and psychologically burdened.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily digital engagement (>5 hours) potentially blurring work-life and social boundaries
Elevated loneliness despite presumably high online connectivity
Notably high anxiety symptoms, the most pronounced of the three distress indicators
Moderate-to-high depressive symptomatology co-occurring with loneliness and anxiety
Pattern consistent with digital overuse that may substitute for rather than supplement meaningful social interaction

label: Emotionally Resilient Graduate Woman
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging approximately 1.21, PHQ-9 depression scores around 0.82, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near 0.79, these individuals fall well below clinical thresholds across all three psychological distress measures, indicating robust emotional well-being.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/social media use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness or social isolation
Maintains moderate and controlled screen or social media use (1–3 hours daily)
Possesses advanced educational attainment, suggesting strong cognitive and social resources
